memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If, however, there is no one to redeem it for them but later on they
prosper and acquire sufficient means to redeem it themselves, they are to
determine the value for the years since they sold it and refund the balance
to the one to whom they sold it; they can then go back to their own
property'" - Lev 25:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Even where no kinsman was available to help, hope was not lost. If the
person's situation improved, they could redeem the land themselves,
calculating a fair price for the remaining years. God's law left the door
of restoration open in more than one way.

There is a gentle realism here. God knew that circumstances change. The
person crushed by poverty this year might recover next year. The law did
not lock people permanently into their worst season.

Dear friend, we can be quick to write off our own situations as permanent.
"This is just how my life is now." "Things will never change." But
seasons genuinely do change, and God is at work in the changing.

Joseph went from a pit to a prison to a palace. Job lost everything and
later saw restoration. Naomi went out empty and came back full. Scripture
is full of turned tides.

This is not a promise that every earthly loss will be reversed in this
life; some are not. But it is a reminder not to treat any hard season as
your final address. James says the Lord is full of compassion and mercy,
pointing to how Job's story ended (Jas 5:11).

Do not carve your current difficulty in stone. Keep the door of hope open,
because God does.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What situation have I written off as permanent?
2. Am I leaving room for God to change my circumstances?
3. How has God turned a hard season for me before?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that seasons change and You are at work in them. Keep me
from despair, and help me hold on to hope through every hard stretch. Amen.
